summary: Explains how TRILL, a protocol that uses IS-IS to forward traffic across multi-hop networks, handles LANs with several RBridges. It describes appointing forwarders so one RBridge handles each VLAN's traffic. It updates RFC 6325, and was replaced by RFC 8139.

eli5.summary: When several guards watch one door, they might all let the same person in. They pick one guard per door to avoid duplicates. This explains how TRILL picks. It was later replaced by RFC 8139.

questions: what is an appointed forwarder in trill
how does the trill designated rbridge appoint forwarders
subtitle: How TRILL picks which RBridge handles native traffic for each VLAN on a shared link, and the timers that keep it loop-safe.

tldr.problem: When several RBridges share one multi-access link, more than one could pick up the same native frames for a VLAN, which can create loops that the TRILL hop count does not protect.
tldr.mechanism: The Designated RBridge (DRB) appoints other RBridges as Appointed Forwarders for ranges of VLANs through sub-TLVs in its TRILL Hellos, and an inhibition mechanism with timers stops a forwarder from handling native frames when another one may be active.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6439 documents this mechanism more fully and updates RFC 6325. It has since been obsoleted by RFC 8139.

facts.label: VLAN inhibition timers
facts.value: Up to 4,094, one per legal VLAN ID

facts.label: Minimum VLAN timers
facts.value: At least two MUST be implemented

today: RFC 6439 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 8139 and updated by RFC 7180. It updates RFC 6325, so current readers should look at RFC 8139 for the up-to-date text.

sections.title: Why Appointed Forwarders Exist
sections.content:
TRILL devices are called RBridges. A link can have several end stations and several RBridges attached. Native traffic to and from the end stations is handled by a subset of those RBridges, the Appointed Forwarders, with the intent that native traffic in each VLAN is handled by at most one RBridge. One RBridge can be Appointed Forwarder for many VLANs.

The purpose of RFC 6439 is to improve the documentation of this mechanism, so it updates RFC 6325. It includes reference implementation details, but other implementations that interoperate on the wire are permitted. If the two documents conflict, RFC 6439 prevails.

The mechanism is irrelevant on links with no end station service, such as point-to-point IS-IS links or links where every RBridge port is a trunk port. It does not affect adjacency formation, the DRB election or pseudonode formation (covered in RFC 6327), and it has no effect on forwarding of TRILL Data frames. It only affects native frames.
sections.eli5: Several grown-ups may stand at one school gate. To avoid two of them letting in the same child, each class gets just one grown-up in charge.

sections.title: Who Is Appointed and Why Only One
sections.content:
The Appointed Forwarder for VLAN-x on a link is the RBridge that ingresses native frames from the link and egresses native frames to the link in VLAN-x. By default the DRB is in charge of native traffic for all VLANs on the link. It may act as Appointed Forwarder for any VLAN itself and may appoint other RBridges with ports on the link.

Two Appointed Forwarders for the same VLAN at the same time could form a loop where frames are not protected by a TRILL hop count. This can even happen with two forwarders for different VLANs if the link maps frames between those VLANs. An RBridge can gain or lose the role in three ways: through DRB elections, by action of the DRB, or by local configuration.

An RBridge that becomes the DRB can act as Appointed Forwarder for any VLANs it chooses, provided its port is not a trunk port and has that VLAN enabled. It loses all Appointed Forwarder status when it loses the DRB role, or when it sees a different RBridge become the DRB. Disabling a VLAN on a port cancels the status for that VLAN, and making a port a trunk or point-to-point port revokes any status that depended on it. Re-enabling a VLAN does not by itself make the RBridge a forwarder.
sections.eli5: The boss guard can work any door, or hand a door to a helper. A guard who stops being the boss, or whose door is closed, loses those doors.

sections.title: How the DRB Appoints Forwarders
sections.content:
The DRB appoints other RBridges by including one or more Appointed Forwarders sub-TLVs in a TRILL Hello sent on the Designated VLAN out the port that won the election. When it sends any appointments, it must send all of them in that Hello. Any previous appointment not included is implicitly revoked. The DRB MUST NOT send appointments unless its DRB inhibition timer for the link has expired. How it chooses whom to appoint is outside the scope of the document.

A non-DRB RBridge checks that a Hello came from the winning DRB port. If not, any appointment sub-TLVs are ignored. If it did, the receiver becomes appointed for the VLANs that are both listed for it and enabled on the receiving port. VLAN IDs 0x000 and 0xFFF are ignored. Any other VLANs it was forwarding for are revoked.

An appointment covers a contiguous range of VLAN IDs. For scattered sets, such as even-numbered VLANs, the network manager can enable only those VLANs on the target port and have the DRB appoint it for all VLANs. Because the Designated VLAN SHOULD be enabled on every RBridge port on the link, the general case needs two appointments. The RFC's example appoints for VLANs 1 through 100 and 102 through 4,094 when the Designated VLAN is 101.

The DRB need not repeat appointments in every Hello, but it is RECOMMENDED that it send them on the Designated VLAN at least once per its Holding Time on the winning port. The RFC estimates that appointments for 83 RBridges fit in under 1000 bytes of a Hello, and it says more than 65 Appointed Forwarders on a link is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: The boss guard hands out a list: who watches which doors. If a guard is not on the new list, they stop watching. The boss tells the list again every so often, just in case.

sections.title: The Inhibition Timers
sections.content:
As a loop-safety backstop, an RBridge keeps timers for every link where it can offer end station service: a DRB inhibition timer, a root change inhibition timer, and up to 4,094 VLAN inhibition timers, one per legal VLAN ID. The first two MUST be implemented. At least two VLAN timers MUST be implemented, and merging them is allowed with care. An RBridge MUST NOT merge the timers of two VLANs if it is the forwarder for one and not the other.

The timers are set by rules. On boot all timers start expired except the DRB timer. Becoming the DRB sets the DRB timer to the Holding Time of the winning port, and losing DRB status sets it to expired. When RB1 receives a Hello claiming the sender is Appointed Forwarder for VLAN-x, it sets its VLAN-x timer to the larger of its current value and the Hello's Holding Time. Enabling a VLAN on a link for the first time sets that VLAN's timer to the port's Holding Time.

On detecting a change in the common spanning tree root, the root change timer is set to a value that defaults to 30 seconds and is configurable from 30 down to zero. The text suggests 7 seconds if Rapid Spanning Tree runs throughout the attached bridged LAN, or 4 seconds with a minimum Bridge Hello Timer. When ports are found to share a link, their timers merge by taking the maximum; when they are found to be on separate links, the timers are cloned.
sections.eli5: Each guard carries a few stopwatches. If any stopwatch is still running, the guard waits instead of acting, because someone else might already be doing the job.

sections.title: Behavior While Inhibited
sections.content:
A forwarder is inhibited for VLAN-x if its DRB inhibition timer, its root change inhibition timer or its VLAN-x inhibition timer has not expired. An inhibited forwarder still decapsulates a TRILL Data frame for VLAN-x, but it does not output or queue the native frame to that link, although it may send it to other links. A native frame received in VLAN-x from that link is ignored except for address learning.

An inhibited RBridge must still say in the Hellos it sends on VLAN-x whether it is Appointed Forwarder for VLAN-x. Inhibition has no effect on receiving or forwarding TRILL Data frames.

An RBridge may have several ports on the same link. Ports suspended for duplicate MAC addresses never ingress or egress native frames. If the RBridge is forwarder for a VLAN across several non-suspended ports, it can share the load however it likes as long as a frame sent out of one port cannot come in on another of its ports. If the DRB sees a Hello sent on VLAN-y arrive in VLAN-x, which shows VLAN mapping, it MUST arrange for the same RBridge to be forwarder for both.
sections.eli5: A waiting guard still reads the signs and keeps telling the others what it would do. It just does not let anyone through until its stopwatches run out.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 6439 provides improved documentation of the Appointed Forwarder mechanism. It does not change the security considerations of the TRILL base protocol, and it points readers to Section 6 of RFC 6325.
sections.eli5: This note only explains the rules more clearly, so it adds no new safety worries beyond the main TRILL rules.

items.title: DRB inhibition timer
items.text: Set to the winning port's Holding Time when an RBridge becomes DRB; expired when it loses DRB status.

items.title: Root change inhibition timer
items.text: Set when the spanning tree root changes; defaults to 30 seconds, configurable from 30 down to zero.

items.title: VLAN inhibition timer
items.text: Per VLAN; extended whenever a Hello says another RBridge is Appointed Forwarder for that VLAN.
